mechanisms.name: win32-lazy-koffi-ffi-binding
mechanisms.what: All Win32 access goes through lazily-resolved Koffi bindings. `bindingContext()` loads `kernel32.dll` and `advapi32.dll` once and returns a `bind` helper that calls `lib.func('__stdcall', name, result, args)`; `bindings()` additionally loads the current process with `koffi.load(null)` to bind `uv_get_osfhandle`, then populates `CurrentTokenProcessBindings` with CloseHandle, GetLastError, FormatMessageW, CreatePipe, SetHandleInformation, CreateProcessAsUserW, CreateProcessW, ReadFile, PeekNamedPipe, WaitForSingleObject, GetExitCodeProcess, CreateJobObjectW, SetInformationJobObject, QueryInformationJobObject, AssignProcessToJobObject, ResumeThread, TerminateProcess, TerminateJobObject and GetStdHandle. `STARTUPINFOW` and `PROCESS_INFORMATION` are declared with `koffi.struct` under the names `DSH_STARTUPINFOW`/`DSH_PROCESS_INFORMATION` and size-asserted against the x64 constants at module load. `extendWin32ProcessBindings(create)` lets a caller (the Windows sandbox) add policy-specific API families over the shared table.
invariants: STARTUPINFOW layout mismatch: koffi computed ${STARTUPINFOW.size}, expected ${abi.STARTUPINFOW_SIZE} — thrown at import when the ABI does not match. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/ffi.ts:159-161)

The sandbox mutates its process environment before this call. Passing an explicit block through Koffi makes CreateProcessAsUserW reject the request with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, so lpEnvironment remains NULL. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:179-181)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a layout mismatch or a failed bind throws at load; every checked Win32 call funnels into `throwLastError`/`throwWin32` which raise `Win32Error`.

constants.meaning: x64 STARTUPINFOW byte size asserted against koffi's computed size
x64 PROCESS_INFORMATION byte size asserted at load
the three loaded modules (null = current process, for uv_get_osfhandle)
FormatMessageW message buffer size in bytes (buffer.length / 2 passed as the character count)

mechanisms.name: win32-job-object-kill-on-close
mechanisms.what: `createKillOnCloseJob(api)` calls `CreateJobObjectW(null, null)` (unnamed), then allocates a `JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_SIZE` (144-byte) buffer and writes `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (`0x00002000`) at byte offset 16, applying it with `SetInformationJobObject(job, JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation /* 9 */, ...)`. On failure it closes the Job handle and throws. `isJobEmpty` queries `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation` (class 1) into a 48-byte buffer and reads `ActiveProcesses` at offset 40. `probeCurrentTokenJobSupport` creates and immediately closes such a Job to prove the current token can use one.
invariants: Job limit that terminates every member when the final Job handle closes. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/abi.ts:31)
Only the KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE limit is set — no CPU/memory/UI limits are configured.
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a failed CreateJobObjectW, SetInformationJobObject or QueryInformationJobObject throws `Win32Error`; `createKillOnCloseJob` closes the Job handle before throwing so no leaked kernel object remains.

constants.meaning: the only Job limit flag set
buffer size for the extended limit record
query class and layout for isJobEmpty

mechanisms.name: win32-suspended-create-assign-resume
mechanisms.what: `spawnJobProcess` is the shared lifecycle for both Job-spawning entry points: create the kill-on-close Job, resolve stdio handles, enable `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` on stdin/stdout/stderr (recording each so the bits can be restored in `finally`), allocate and encode a `STARTUPINFOW` with `cb = 104` and `dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES`, create the process with `CREATE_SUSPENDED` (plus `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` for the current-token path), then `AssignProcessToJobObject(job, hProcess)` and finally `ResumeThread(hThread)`. Every failure step terminates the process (exit code 1) and closes the Job, thread and process handles before throwing. `spawnInheritedJobProcess` uses `CreateProcessAsUserW` with the restricted token and the runner's own `GetStdHandle` values; `spawnCurrentTokenJobProcess` uses `CreateProcessW` with the resolved `applicationName`, a UTF-16 environment block, and target handle values obtained from `uv_get_osfhandle` on the carrier descriptors.
invariants: Node clears stdio handle inheritability at startup through uv_disable_stdio_inheritance. This operation temporarily restores the bits required by STARTF_USESTDHANDLES. Restoring them afterward is best-effort: failure must not replace the already-created child's outcome. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:494-497)
The runner spawns nothing else; cleanup failure must not mask the child. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:443)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a null process/thread handle pair, a failed Job assignment, or a failed ResumeThread throws after killing the just-created process (`TerminateProcess(hProcess, 1)`), so a Job member can never escape unowned.

constants.meaning: creation flag for both Job spawn paths
bit set before create and cleared after (process.ts:420, :444)
uv_get_osfhandle failure sentinels rejected by targetCarrierHandles

mechanisms.name: win32-command-line-and-environment-encoding
mechanisms.what: `quoteArg` implements the `CommandLineToArgvW` backslash/quote rules: an empty argument becomes `""`, an argument without whitespace or quotes is passed bare, and otherwise a quoted form doubles runs of backslashes before a quote and before the terminating quote. `buildCommandLine` maps `quoteArg` over `[program, ...args]` and joins with spaces. `encodeWindowsEnvironment` sorts entries by case-folded key and emits `key=value` strings joined by `\0` with a double-NUL terminator, encoded `utf16le` into a Buffer that `CreateProcessW` receives as `lpEnvironment`.
invariants: Quote one argument according to CommandLineToArgvW parsing. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:21)
The environment block is emitted double-NUL-terminated and case-insensitively sorted, matching the Win32 requirement.
mechanisms.failurePolicy: n/a (pure encoding) — no failure path; a malformed argv simply produces the corresponding Win32 command line.

constants.meaning: test that decides whether quoting is needed at all

mechanisms.name: win32-anonymous-pipe-capture
mechanisms.what: `spawnPipedProcess(api, options)` creates three anonymous pipes via `CreatePipe(readHandle, writeHandle, null, 0)`, sets `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` on the child-side ends (stdin read, stdout write, stderr write), encodes a `STARTUPINFOW` pointing at them, and creates the process through `CreateProcessAsUserW` with `lpEnvironment = null` and a restricted primary token. On success it closes the parent-side ends it no longer needs and hands back the process handle plus the stdout/stderr read ends. `drainPipe` peeks with `PeekNamedPipe`, reads available bytes with `ReadFile`, yields 1 ms between polls, terminates on `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` (109) or `ERROR_NO_DATA` (232), and always closes the handle in `finally`. `waitForProcessExit` waits with `INFINITE` and always closes the process handle.
invariants: The sandbox mutates its process environment before this call ... so lpEnvironment remains NULL. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:179-181)
Drain one anonymous pipe until the writer closes it ... the handle is always closed. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:273-278)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — every failed Win32 call throws `Win32Error` (via `throwLastError`/`throwWin32`); the catch path runs `closeAllOwned` so all pipes created so far are closed before the error propagates.

constants.value: PeekNamedPipe return 0 with ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE (109) or ERROR_NO_DATA (232)

mechanisms.name: win32-process-and-job-polling
mechanisms.what: `pollProcessExit(api, process)` performs a zero-time `WaitForSingleObject`: `WAIT_TIMEOUT` (258) means still running and returns undefined, `0xFFFFFFFF` throws, anything else reads the exit code with `GetExitCodeProcess` and returns it. `isJobEmpty(api, job)` queries `JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation` and returns true only when `ActiveProcesses` (offset 40 in the 48-byte record) is zero. Together these are what the Windows Job runner polls on its 10 ms timer, and `closeHandleChecked(api, handle, detail)` centralizes checked handle closure with a labeled error.
invariants: Poll one process handle without blocking the runner event loop. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:552)
Return whether a Job has no active processes. (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:571)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an unexpected wait result, a failed GetExitCodeProcess, a failed QueryInformationJobObject, or a failed CloseHandle all throw `Win32Error` with the API name.

mechanisms.name: win32-error-surfacing
mechanisms.what: `Win32Error extends Error` carries the exact failing `api` name and the `win32Code`, with message `${api} failed (Win32 ${win32Code})[: detail]`. `errorText(api, win32Code)` renders the system message through `FormatMessageW` with `FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM | FORMAT_MESSAGE_IGNORE_INSERTS` into a 1024-byte buffer, decoding `utf16le` and trimming (empty string when the call returns 0). `throwLastError(api, name, detail?)` captures the CURRENT `GetLastError()` value and throws; `throwWin32(api, name, win32Code, detail?)` throws an explicitly captured code — used where a cleanup call would otherwise overwrite the error.
invariants: throwWin32 exists so an error captured BEFORE cleanup is the one reported (see the SetInformationJobObject and AssignProcessToJobObject call sites, packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:347-349 and :471-476).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — this module is the failure path; it always throws, never returns a sentinel.

constants.meaning: exported for callers that size a buffer from a Win32 query

subprocess/win32-process.note: Real logic and NOT Cordis plumbing: there is no `Service` subclass, no `apply(ctx)` and no `Context` registration anywhere in the package — `index.ts` is a pure re-export barrel (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/index.ts:1-38). Mechanisms: win32-lazy-koffi-ffi-binding, win32-job-object-kill-on-close, win32-suspended-create-assign-resume, win32-command-line-and-environment-encoding, win32-anonymous-pipe-capture, win32-process-and-job-polling, win32-error-surfacing. Note the split of responsibilities: this package owns the Job Object itself and the suspended-create/assign/resume ladder; packages/subprocess/subprocess-local owns the runner process that drives it and the Toolhelp32 process-table inspector.

notes: All 5 .ts files read in full. Facts to carry into the inventory: (1) Job termination is implemented three ways here — `terminateJob`/`TerminateJobObject` (process.ts:596-598), kill-on-close via the Job limit (process.ts:333-352), and per-process `TerminateProcess` on failure paths. (2) The Job is unnamed and created per spawn (`CreateJobObjectW(null, null)`). (3) `spawnPipedProcess` (restricted-token, piped stdout/stderr) is exported but the ordinary Windows path used by subprocess-local is `spawnCurrentTokenJobProcess`; the piped variant's production caller (if any) is outside this package. (4) `quoteArg`/`buildCommandLine` are exported and used by both job spawn paths (process.ts:235, :503, :525).
